discovery: Theoretical foundation and experimental realization of quantum computation and quantum simulation with trapped ions

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI Innsbruck, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Rainer Blatt
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI Innsbruck, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed that a string of laser-cooled ions, coupled through their collective motion, could carry out universal quantum logic. Their proposal turned quantum computation from an abstract idea into a concrete physical programme. Blatt and his Innsbruck team then realized it step by step: the Cirac-Zoller gate, deterministic teleportation, multi-qubit entanglement, digital and analog quantum simulation of many-body spin models, and error-corrected logical qubits. Cirac and Zoller also founded the wider paradigm of analog quantum simulation, including the proposal that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Hubbard model. Today that paradigm drives quantum simulation across atomic, condensed-matter and high-energy physics. The 2025 prize recognized macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits. This nomination recognizes the complementary microscopic route: controlling individual atoms and their entanglement to engineer and program quantum matter, which has become a pillar of quantum science and technology.
